newsitem.title: PERU: Peru government preparing package of new laws.
newsitem.headline: Peru government preparing package of new laws.

text.p: The Peruvian government is preparing a package of new laws which it hopes to decree under an extension of special powers granted by Congress, officials said Wednesday.
The legislature will debate Thursday whether to accept President Alberto Fujimori's request for a 30-day extension of powers to decree a wide range of political, economic and financial legislation.

Congress President Victor Joy Way, speaking to foreign correspondents, said Wednesday the general extension of powers would likely be granted, although the legislature might reserve the right to formulate a new law governing the bank system.

The government is currently working under special legislative powers granted by Congress for 90 days, but this runs out on Saturday. Among the most important measures being drawn up by the government are laws to:
- Free prisoners wrongly jailed on terrorism charges.
- Create a commercial "corridor" in southern Peru.
- Restructure private private companies' tax debts.
- Update regulations covering the local stock market in order to unify the types of shares being traded.
- Update the regulations covering the pension sector.
Government officials insist these laws are necessary as part of the administration of President Alberto Fujimori's second stage of reforms.
Joy said the special powers of decree were being granted only for the most detailed and complicated legislation, which required government specialists.
He added that the Congress retained a power of veto if it considered any of the decrees proposed by the government.
However, the administration controls 70 seats in the 120- member single-chamber Congress.

Joy said the new banks' law would seek to increase solvency in the financial system, boost saving, strengthen the Superintendency of Banks and Insurance, and raise local regulations to international levels.

Although the government has not revealed all the legislation it is preparing, officials said it was likely a new agriculture law would be also be decreed if Congress granted an extension of special powers.
This law would consolidate property titles and open the agriculture sector to new loans, the officials said.
